newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium jumps.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, palladium jumps.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mixed on Wednesday, with most palladium futures rising by their 24 yen per gram daily limits on animated short-covering by private investors, traders said.
All palladium futures hit their life-of-contract highs on Wednesday, with benchmark June ending up 24 yen at 636 yen.

"In overseas markets on Tuesday, fund buying overwhelmed Russian palladium sales in the spot market, which showed how bullish the market is, forcing TOCOM private investors to cover their short positions," one analyst at a commodity broker said. They said massive short positions in TOCOM remained.
Despite the recent rise in TOCOM palladium futures, the market remained far below dollar-based palladium prices and the wide gap made traders wary of arbitrage dealings.

The TOCOM said on Wednesday it will widen the daily price limit on TOCOM palladium futures to 36 yen per gram effective Thursday, compared with the current limit of 24 yen in view of the sharp gains recently.
Platinum futures opened weaker on profit taking due to losses in New York overnight, but the stronger performance in palladium spilled over into the platinum market.
Benchmark June platinum was up 17 yen at 1,455 yen.
Gold futures settled narrowly mixed on Wednesday with prices ranging from one yen per gram lower to four yen up. Benchmark June was ended up three at 1,229 yen.
"In gold futures, mixed trade was detected. Focus is on whether the dollar will climb above 120 yen," one trader said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $326.00/50 per ounce at 0804 GMT, against $325.70/326.30 in New York on Tuesday.
Silver futures were mostly lower, with benchmark June finishing down 0.1 yen per 10 grams at 169.5 yen.
